answer.rationale: Hard constraint is no added delivery risk with the line at 94% and zero buffer while the primary contract lapses in 14 days without auto-renew. That rules out deferral (c5 was a non-critical month-to-month case, not this expiry), a primary switch (c2 savings and quick onboarding are not evidence a no-buffer 14-day cutover is safe), and adding a second source (does not replace the expiring primary in one decision). Negotiation is already refused this cycle, so c4 does not apply. Renewing the incumbent is the only single action that preserves continuity (c1); it does not deliver the 18% spend cut, which is flagged as residual cost/lock-in risk rather than treated as solved.
